output.summary: Incidents rose far beyond what a 7% volume increase explains, and the rise is not a tool artifact (SEV1-2 are declared manually, and degraded minutes and SLA credits rose). The evidence supports a self-reinforcing loop. Interrupt work displaced reliability work. Overdue postmortem items then recurred as incidents, and 60% of Q3 incidents were repeats. Storage's exemption worked as a natural experiment. Networking's second on-call slot did not help and raised burden. The hiring freeze worsened on-call frequency but did not start the rise. Attrition is confounded between pay and on-call. Prefer ring-fencing engineers to close recurring action items. Avoid the second slot and incident-count targets. Treat pay-only spending as premature.
